In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Commentary on Surat al-Mu'minun, and it is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Successful indeed are the believers﴾. Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Yunus ibn Sulaym, from al-Zuhri, from Urwa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd al-Qari, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "When revelation descended upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), we would hear near his face a buzzing like the buzzing of bees. Once revelation came down to him and we remained for a while. When it had lifted from him, he faced the qibla and said: 'O Allah, honour us and do not humiliate us, give to us and do not deprive us, be pleased with us and be pleased with us, prefer us and do not prefer others over us.' Then he said: 'Ten verses have been revealed to me; whoever observes them will enter Paradise,' and he recited: ﴿Successful indeed are the believers﴾ to the end of the ten." The Shaykh, the Imam, said: This hadith was related to us by Abd al-Rahman ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Siraj informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahbub informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Surah informed us, who said: Abd ibn Humayd informed us, from Abd al-Razzaq... the hadith.

His saying: ﴿Qad aflaha﴾ means: he has prospered, succeeded and attained success. Some of them said: he attained lasting permanence and blessing. The poet said:

(We alighted in lands that all others had alighted in before us, and we hope for goodness after 'Ad and Himyar.)

It was also read "qad uflih al-mu'minun," meaning: proceed to that in which there is goodness.

Labid said in verse:

(Then understand, if you are of those who understand,
and indeed he has prospered who has reason.)

Another said:

(Had any living being been able to attain success, the playing lances would have attained it.)

Ibn Abbas said: they attained what they sought, and were saved from what they fled from.

His saying: ﴿al-mu'minun﴾ means: those who affirm the truth (al-musaddiqun).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 2:

And His saying: ﴿Those who are humble in their prayer﴾, that is: submissive and fearful. It is said: khushu' (humility, reverence) is the fear of the heart, and its reality is attentiveness in prayer toward one's Worshipped Lord and humbling oneself before Him. It is also said: it is the gathering of one's resolve and the warding off of distractions from the prayer, and reflecting upon what passes over the tongue of recitation, glorification (tasbih), declaration of God's oneness (tahlil), and magnification (takbir). From 'Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: khushu' is that one does not turn to his right or to his left during the prayer.

And from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to raise their eyes toward the sky during the prayer. When the words of God, the Exalted, were revealed: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded, those who are humble in their prayer﴾, they cast their eyes toward the places of prostration. And from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, who said: it is tranquility (sukun) in the prayer.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 3:

And His saying: ﴿And those who turn away from vain talk﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it means doubt (al-shakk). Al-Hasan said: all acts of disobedience (al-ma'asi). Al-Zajjaj mentioned that vain talk (al-laghw) is every false speech that is discarded. It is also said that vain talk here is the opposition of the disbelievers with abuse and insult, and this is a good view, because God the Exalted said: ﴿When they pass by vain talk, they pass by with dignity﴾. That is, when they hear foul speech, they honour themselves by refraining from engaging in it.

Allah the Exalted's words: ﴿And those who are active in giving zakah﴾, i.e., those who pay it.

Al-Sha'bi said: it is the zakat al-fitr (the charity of breaking the fast at the end of Ramadan). Others among them said: zakah here means righteous deeds, as if He had said: "And those who are active in righteous deeds."
The words of God Most High: ﴿And those who guard their private parts﴾. Guarding the private parts is abstaining from what is forbidden.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 6:

And His saying: ﴿except from their wives﴾. It is said: the verse refers to men, as evidence that Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿or what their right hands possess﴾, and a woman is not permitted to enjoy what her right hand possesses. It was also said: the beginning of the verse refers to both men and women, and His saying: ﴿or what their right hands possess﴾ refers to men only, not women. ﴿Then they are not blameworthy﴾, meaning: not reproached. If it is asked: if a man has intercourse with his wife during menstruation or postpartum bleeding, or something similar, and likewise with the slave-girl, then he has committed something forbidden, and if he has guarded his private parts from other than his wife and his right hand's possession, will he still be blameworthy? The answer to this: the sense of the verse here is: "And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or what their right hands possess, in a manner that is permitted by the Sharia, then they are not blameworthy." The same is the answer to the one who has used this verse as evidence for the permissibility of approaching a woman in other than the place of approach, or a slave-girl.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 7:

And His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿So whoever seeks beyond that, it is those who are the transgressors.﴾ (i.e., other than that. "Ibtagha" means: sought, desired. And His saying: ﴿it is those who are the transgressors﴾ means: the wrongdoers who go beyond the lawful to the unlawful.) The scholars have used this verse as evidence that masturbation by hand (istimna' bil-yad) is forbidden. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he was asked about it, and he said: "It is a man's committing a sin against himself (nā'ik nafsahu)." It is related from Ibn Jurayj that he said: "I asked 'Ata' about it, and he said: 'It is disliked (makruh).' I said: 'Is there a legal penalty (hadd) for it?' He said: 'I have not heard of one.'" It is related from Salim ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar that he was asked about this act, and he said: "Uff, uff! I have heard that some people will be raised on the Day of Resurrection with their hands pregnant, so I think they are these." It is related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he said: "Allah punished a nation among the nations who used to toy with their private parts." Malik and al-Shafi'i disliked it. Abu 'Asim al-Nabil related from Abu Hanifa that he disliked it, but if one places a piece of silk between his hand and his penis, he said: "There is no harm in it." Al-Naqqash mentioned in his tafsir, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, that he said: "Those are people who have no share (in the good)."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 8:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who are faithful to their trusts and their covenants﴾. It is said: "raʿā kadhā" (he attended to such-and-such) when he undertook the welfare of it. From this is his saying (ﷺ): "Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock." It is said of the ruler: "He is a rāʿī (shepherd/guardian)," because he attends to the welfare of the subjects. The meaning of ﴿rāʿūn﴾ here is the discharge of trusts and the fulfilment of covenants.

Almost "Commentary of al-Sam'ani" — translating the passage:

God Most High says: ﴿And those who are steadfast in their prayers﴾. We have already explained the meaning of al-muḥāfaẓah (steadfastness, guarding). It is related from Ibn Mas'ud that he was asked about al-muḥāfaẓah, and he said: "Guarding the time." It was then said to him: "And what of one who abandons it altogether?" He said: "That is disbelief (kufr)."

He repeated the mention of the prayer here in order to make clear that steadfastness in it is obligatory, just as humility (khushu') in it is obligatory.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 10–11:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Those are the inheritors who will inherit al-Firdaws (the highest garden)﴾. It is related by al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet said: "There is not one of you except that he has a dwelling in Paradise and a dwelling in Hell. When he enters Hell, the people of Paradise inherit his dwelling."

And from Mujahid, he said: "When he enters Paradise, his dwelling in Hell is demolished." And from him (Mujahid) also, he said: "Indeed, Allah planted the Garden of Eden with His own hand, then said: ﴿The believers have certainly prospered﴾, and closed it off. None enters it except whom Allah wills, and its gate is opened every dawn, and they used to say that the breeze of the dawn comes from it."

And in some of the collections of hadith (masanid): from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet: "Allah created the Garden of Eden, and created in it what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Then He said to it: 'Speak.' It said: ﴿The believers have certainly prospered﴾. 'I am forbidden to every miser and show-off.'"

And in another narration: "Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The believers have certainly prospered﴾, then He said: 'By My might, no miser shall be my neighbour in you.'"

And in some of the masanid also, from the Prophet, he said: "Allah the Exalted created Adam with His hand, planted the Garden of Eden with His hand, and wrote the Torah with His hand. Then He said to the Garden of Eden: 'By My might, no miser and no cuckold shall dwell in you.'"

And in some of the tafsir works: that the Prophet said: "Allah the Exalted created al-Firdaws and made for it a brick of gold and a brick of silver, and its mortar (hubaluha) is pure musk." All these reports are strange (gharib). ﴿They will abide therein forever﴾, i.e., they will remain and never depart.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 10–11:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Those are the inheritors who will inherit al-Firdaws (the highest garden)﴾. It is related by al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet said: "There is not one of you except that he has a dwelling in Paradise and a dwelling in Hell. Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 12:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿And We indeed created man from an extract of clay﴾. The people of language (ahl al-lughah) said: al-sulalah (extract) is the choicest of water poured out (al-masul) from the loins. As for His saying ﴿from clay﴾, the clay here is Adam, and most of the scholars held this view, and the intended meaning of "man" is his offspring. Some said: the intended meaning of "man" is Adam himself. As for His saying ﴿from an extract﴾, meaning: extracted from every soil. Al-Kalbi said: al-sulalah here is the clay which, when a man grasps it, water comes out from the two sides of his hand. Mujahid reported: it is the semen of the children of Adam. The poet said:

(Is Hind but a well-bred Arab mare, [an offspring] of stallions, whom a mule has covered?)

(If she gives birth to a colt, then praise be to God for her; but if she bears a mule, the mule has come by it.)

And His saying: ﴿Then We placed him as a drop (nutfah) in a firm resting place (qarar makin)﴾, meaning: in a place in which he settled. It is related from Mujahid that he said: "There is no drop (nutfah) except that some of the dust from which he was created is scattered upon it."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 14:

And His saying: ﴿Then We made the drop into a clinging clot﴾. Al-'alaqah is a piece of blood.

And His saying: ﴿Then We made the clinging clot into a lump of flesh﴾. Al-mudghah is a piece of flesh.

And His saying: ﴿Then We made the lump into bones﴾. It is also read as "izaman" (ʿiẓāman), and the meaning is one. The poet said:

(In their throats there is a bone, and we have been wounded...)

That is: in their throats there are bones.

It is said that between each of the two creations there are forty days.

And His saying: ﴿Then We clothed the bones with flesh﴾, meaning: We put on (them).

And His saying: ﴿Then We produced it as another creation﴾. Most of them hold that what is meant by it is the breathing of the spirit into it. Al-Dahhak said: the reaching of youth. From Qatadah, he said: the growth of the teeth. From al-Hasan: male or female. In some tafsirs it is said that God breathes the spirit into it after four months and ten days from the day the drop falls into the womb, and for this reason the waiting period of widowhood is determined by this length of time.

And His saying: ﴿So blessed is God, the best of creators﴾. It is related that when ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, heard this verse, (he said: "So blessed is God, the best of creators." The Prophet said: "Thus it was revealed.") If it is said: this verse indicates that we create our own actions, since God the Exalted said: ﴿So blessed is God, the best of creators﴾, mentioning "the creators" in the plural form? The answer: its meaning is "the best of those who measure," and khalq has come in the sense of taqdir (measuring). The poet said:

(Indeed you measure what you cut out, while some of the people cut out and then do not measure.) [That is]: measure.

It is also said: its meaning is: they make, and I make, and I am the best of makers.

"The saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Then indeed, after that, you will surely die.﴾ Some of them said: al-mayyit and al-mayyit are one and the same. Others said: al-mayyit is the one who has already died, and al-mayyit is the one who will die in the future; and similar to it is al-ma'it. This is like what they say: sayyid and sa'id, the latter being one who will become a lord (sayyid) in the future."

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, will be raised up.﴾ Al-ba'th (resurrection, raising up) is release (al-itlaq), as if they had been held back for a period and then released.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 17:

His saying: ﴿And We have created above you seven paths﴾. Al-ṭarā'iq (the paths) here are the heavens. Regarding calling them "paths" there are two views. The first: they were called paths because some of them are above others; it is said: "ṭāraqtu al-na'l" (I placed one sandal above another) when one places some of them over others.

The second view: they were called paths because they are the paths of the angels.

And His saying: ﴿And We were not unaware of the creation﴾, meaning: We are its guardians. It is said: "We kept the sky from falling upon them." And it is said: "We did not leave them neglected, without a command or a prohibition."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 18:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We sent down water from the sky in a measured amount﴾. In the report: "Allah, may He be exalted, sent down four rivers from Paradise: Sayhan, Jayhan, the Tigris (Dijla), and the Euphrates (al-Furat)."

It is also narrated that He sent down five rivers from a spring in Paradise. Along with the four we have mentioned, He included the Nile of Egypt (Nil Misr). In this report, Allah placed them in the mountains and then made them flow for the benefit of the servants. Also in this report: "When Gog and Magog emerge, Allah will lift up the Qur'an, the Ka'bah, the Black Stone (al-Rukn), the Station of Abraham (al-Maqam), the Ark of Moses, and the five rivers, and nothing of the good of this world and the Hereafter will remain." This is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed, We are able to take it away﴾.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then We produced for you therewith gardens of date palms and grapevines; in them you have abundant fruits, and from them you eat.﴾ The meaning is apparent. The date palms and grapevines are singled out for mention because they were the most common fruits of the Arabs.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 20:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And a tree that springs forth from Mount Sinai﴾. Its meaning: We produced a tree that springs forth from Mount Sinai, and it is the olive tree. He singled it out for mention because it does not need orchards (ma'ahid, i.e., cultivated enclosures), so the blessing in it is greater; and because it is eaten and used for lighting lamps (mustasbah). His saying: ﴿Sina'* (Sinai)﴾, in Abyssinian (Habashi), means "the good." As for what is related from Ibn 'Abbas, there are two meanings: the first is that what is meant by Sina' is blessing, and its meaning is "the mountain of blessing"; the second is that its meaning is "the trees," i.e., the mountain full of trees. This was reported by al-Kalbi.

His saying: ﴿grows with oil﴾. It is also read "tunbitu" (with a damma on the ta'). Scholars differed regarding this. Some said: anbata and nabata have the same meaning. The poet said:

(I saw the people of need around their tents, / Settled with them until the herbage sprouted [anbata al-baql])

He means: until the herbage grew (nabata al-baql). So the meaning according to this is "grows with oil," that is: along with it is the oil, or in it is the oil. Abu 'Ubayda said: the ba' (bi) is superfluous (za'ida), so the meaning according to this is: it grows the fruit of oil.

As for those who distinguished between tanbitu and tunbitu, they said its meaning is: it produces its fruit with oil (tunbitu thamaraha bi-l-duhn), and it grows the fruit of oil (tanbitu thamara al-duhn).

They cited poetry for the addition of the ba': (black-eyed, not reciting the surahs with...)

That is: they do not recite the surahs.

His saying: ﴿and a condiment for those who eat﴾. It is also read "wa-sibagh li-l-akilin" (with sibagh), which is a shadhdh (irregular) reading, like libs and libas. Its meaning is "and a relish (idam) for those who eat," for when bread is dipped in it, it takes on its color (insabagha bihi, in the sense of taluwwun). The idam is everything eaten along with bread customarily, whether or not the bread takes on its color. It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he took a morsel of bread and a date and said: "This is the relish of that."

And it is related from him (ﷺ) that he said: "The best relish of the people of Paradise is meat."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 21:

Allah's saying: ﴿And indeed, in the cattle there is a lesson for you﴾ means: the sign (ayah) in them, by which you take heed.

And His saying: ﴿We give you to drink of what is in their bellies﴾ means: the milk.

And His saying: ﴿And for you in them are many benefits, and from them you eat﴾ means: from their meat.
﴿And upon them and upon the ship you are carried.﴾ The meaning is apparent.

The Almighty's saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, and he said, "O my people, worship Allah"﴾. That is: affirm the oneness of Allah.

﴿You have no god other than Him﴾. That is: no one worthy of worship besides Him. And His saying: ﴿Will you not then be wary?﴾ means: Will you not fear His punishment if you worship other than Him?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 24:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So the chiefs of those among his people who disbelieved said, "This is none but a human being like you."﴾ We have already mentioned the meaning of al-Mala' (the chiefs, the notables), and we have mentioned their denial of the sending of a human being.

And His words: ﴿He wants to assert superiority over you.﴾ Yatafaddal means: he displays superiority, while he has no superiority, just as one says: "So-and-so yatahallam" (feigns forbearance), meaning he displays forbearance while he has no forbearance, and "yatazarraf" (feigns wit), meaning he displays wit while he has no wit.

And His words: ﴿If Allah had willed, He would have sent down angels.﴾ That is, to convey the revelation. And His words: ﴿We never heard of this among our forefathers of old.﴾ That is, [we never heard of] the sending of a human being as a messenger. It was also said: [we never heard of] a call like his call.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He is only a man in whom there is madness﴾, meaning: insanity (junun).

And His saying: ﴿So wait for him for a while﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: until some time. It is also said: until he dies.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He said, "My Lord, support me, for they have denied me."﴾ That is, destroy them as a victory for me, as recompense for their denial.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 27:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We revealed to him, "Build the ship under Our eyes and Our inspiration."﴾ We have already explained this before. It is said: he planted the trees for forty years and dried them for forty years.

His saying: ﴿So when Our command comes and the oven boils over﴾ The intended meaning of "the command" here is the time of their drowning, and the tannur (oven) is the baker's oven. We have explained other than this before.

His saying: ﴿Then load into it two of each pair﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said its meaning is: two of every kind, two by two.

His saying: ﴿And your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth among them﴾ That is, those against whom the judgment of destruction has already gone forth, and he is the son of Noah. Al-Hasan said: they were seven, and the eighth of them was Noah. It is also said: they were six, and the seventh of them was Noah.

His saying: ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are to be drowned.﴾ We have already explained this.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 28:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then when you have settled, you and whoever is with you, in the ark﴾ means: you have become settled and seated. The word istiwa' may also mean "rising up" (irtifa'). Al-Khalil (al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Farahidi) said: We entered upon Abu Rabi'ah al-A'rabi, and he said to us: "Istawu," meaning: rise up.

And His saying: ﴿Then say: "All praise is for Allah, who has saved us from the wrongdoing people"﴾ means: from the disbelieving people. In some reports from the Prophet (ﷺ) it is related that he said: "The likeness of my family is like the ark of Noah: whoever boards it is saved, and whoever does not board it perishes."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 23, verse 29:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And say, "My Lord, cause me to disembark at a blessed place, and You are the best of those who bring to rest."﴾ It is also read as "manzalan" (منزلا). The manzil (منزل) is the place of alighting (nuzul), and the manzil may also mean the act of causing to alight (inzal). Regarding the place of alighting there are two opinions: the first is that it is the ship after boarding, and the second is that it is the land after disembarking from the ship. The blessing after disembarking is the abundance of offspring from his three sons, and the blessing before disembarking is deliverance (najah).

In some reports from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever alights at a place and says, 'My Lord, cause me to disembark at a blessed place, and You are the best of those who bring to rest,' it shall be a guarantee upon Allah that He will protect him from everything that frightens him, and if he dies in that place he will enter Paradise." Ibn Faris mentioned it in his tafsir on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, and the report is gharib (strange, i.e., weakly transmitted with a single narrator at some point in its chain).

Allah's saying: ﴿Indeed in that are signs, and indeed We were ever testing.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: [We were] testing whoever obeyed and whoever disobeyed. And from another source he said its meaning is: There is no nation but that We have tested it.
Al-Sam'ani's commentary on the verse: His words, "Then We produced after them another generation" (i.e., another people).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 32:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Then We sent among them a messenger from themselves﴾. In the interpretation (tafsir) it is said that the "qarn" (generation) are the people of Hud, and they are ʿAd, and the messenger is Hud. It is also said: they are the people of Salih, and the messenger is Salih. The first view is more sound and more evident.

And His words: ﴿Worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. Will you not then be wary (of Him)?﴾ We have already mentioned it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 33:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And the chiefs of his people who disbelieved and denied the meeting of the Hereafter said﴾. That is: with the return to the Hereafter.

And His words: ﴿and whom We had given luxury in the life of this world﴾. That is: and whom We had made wealthy in the life of this world. It is also said: We had widened their livelihood in the life of this world, until they became affluent. And al-itraf (luxury) is indulgence in the delights of living. Al-Qutabi said: al-tarfah is like al-tuhfah (a gift).

And His words: ﴿This is none but a human like you; he eats of what you eat, and drinks of what you drink﴾. He means: of it (i.e., "mimma" means "of that which").

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 34:

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And if you obey a human being like yourselves﴾ means: made of flesh and blood like yourselves.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, you would then surely be losers﴾ means: the defrauded (al-maghbunun). It is also said: those who abandon the way of the intelligent, so you would be like one who has lost his intellect.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 35:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Does he promise you that when you die and become dust and bones, you will be brought forth?﴾

The summary of the meaning: "Does he promise you that when you die and are buried, then you will be brought out from your graves?" In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is: "Does he promise you, when you die and become dust and bones, that you will be brought forth?" As for the well-known reading, the first "anna" is in the accusative by way of the implied preposition "bi" (meaning "that"), i.e., "bi-annakum," and the second "innakum" is for emphasis. Al-Zajjaj said: A parallel to this in the Qur'an is the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Do they not know that whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger, for him is the fire of Hell?﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 36:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Far, far is that which you are promised.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: its meaning is: far, far is what you are promised, that is, it will never happen, ever. Hayhat (far, far) and Ayhat (far, far) have one meaning. The poet said:

(Ayhat, ayhat is al-ʿAqiq and its people... ayhat, ayhat is a friend with whom we would join at al-ʿAqiq.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 37:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There is nothing but our life of this world; we die and we live﴾. If it is said: How can His saying ﴿and we live﴾ be right, when they did not affirm the resurrection (ba'th)? The answer is in several respects. The first: it is according to inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir), meaning: "we live and we die." The second: the fathers die and the sons live. The third: some people die and some people live.

His saying: ﴿And we are not to be resurrected﴾, meaning: not to be gathered (bi-munsharin).

Translation:

And His words: ﴿He is only a man who has invented a lie against Allah, and we are not believers in him﴾ — meaning: we are not those who affirm him as true.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 23, verse 39:

God's words: ﴿He said: "My Lord, help me, for they have denied me."﴾ We have already explained this.

His saying: ﴿He said, "In a little while they will surely become regretful."﴾ Meaning: *la-yusbihūna nādimīn* (they will become regretful), and the meaning of *yuṣbiḥūn* is *yaṣīrūn* (they will become).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 41:

His statement, the Exalted: ﴿So the Cry seized them in truth﴾. Regarding the story: Jibril (peace be upon him) cried out at them with a cry, and their hearts were split apart.

It is also said that what is meant by the Cry is destruction. Imru' al-Qays said:

(Leave aside the prohibition that was cried out in its chambers... rather, the tale is the tale of the riding camels)

ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) quoted this verse during some of his battles.

His statement: ﴿in truth﴾, i.e., with justice. It is also said: for what they deserved.

His statement: ﴿So We made them debris (ghuthaʾ)﴾. Ghuthaʾ is what has dried up of trees and grass and floated on top of the flood. It is also said that ghuthaʾ is foam, and foam is of no benefit and passes away as nothing, so He likened them after destruction to it.

His statement: ﴿So away with the wrongdoing people﴾, i.e., destruction to the wrongdoing people.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 42:

His saying: ﴿Then We brought into being after them other generations﴾, meaning: other peoples.

Al-Sam'ani's commentary on Surah 23, verse 43:

His words, ﴿No community can precede its term﴾, mean: the time of their destruction.

And his words, ﴿nor can they delay﴾, mean: they cannot be delayed beyond the time of their destruction.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 44:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then We sent Our messengers in succession.﴾ It is recited "tatra" with tanwin (tatrā), and the meaning is: following one another in succession. It is said: between every two prophets there is an interval of time. The original form of ﴿tatra﴾ is "watra" (watrā), except that the waw was changed into a ta', so it is as if He said: We sent the messengers one after another, singly, one after another.

And His saying: ﴿Every time a nation's messenger came to them, they denied him.﴾ That is, they rejected him and disavowed him.

And His saying: ﴿So We made them follow one another [to destruction].﴾ That is, in destruction.

And His saying: ﴿And We made them into tales.﴾ That is, into objects of evening talk and stories. One of them said in verse:

(So be a good tale for others to recount… for people are only tales.)

And His saying: ﴿So away with the people who do not believe.﴾ This has already been explained.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 45:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then We sent Musa and his brother Harun with Our signs and a manifest authority﴾. That is: with a clear proof, which are the nine signs.

Almighty God's words: ﴿To Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they waxed arrogant, for they were a haughty people﴾. That is, they were seeking exaltedness without right. Arrogance (istikbar) is the seeking of pride (takabbur). It is also said: ﴿haughty﴾ means dominating, overpowering those beneath them through oppression.

And the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So they said, "Shall we believe in two humans like ourselves?"﴾ That is, Musa and Harun. And His saying: ﴿while their people are servants to us?﴾ Abu 'Ubayda said: The Arabs say of anyone who obeys a person that he has worshipped him.

And in some works of tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis): the Copts used to worship Pharaoh, and Pharaoh used to worship an idol.
"Then they denied them both, and so they were among those destroyed." — i.e., by drowning.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book that they might be guided﴾. That is, the Tawrah (the Torah).

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 23, verse 50:

His saying: ﴿And We made the son of Maryam and his mother a sign﴾ has already been explained.

And His saying: ﴿And We sheltered them on a high ground﴾. It is also read as "rubwah" (rubwa). Abu al-Ashhab al-Uqayli read it as "rabawah". As for al-Rabwah (the high ground), there are several opinions. From Abu Hurayrah, who said: "It is the sandy plain of Palestine (Ramlat Filastin)," and this was narrated with a chain going back to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: "It is the Ghawtah of Damascus." (It is said: the most pleasant places in the world are four: the Ghawtah of Damascus in Syria, al-Ayla in Iraq, Shi'b Bawan in Persia, and Sa'd in Samarqand.) From Ka'b, who said: "﴿Rabwah﴾ is Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem)." From Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: "It is Egypt." In the lexicon, al-Rabwah is an elevated place.

His saying: ﴿with a settled place﴾, meaning: level land where they can settle. It was also said: level, elevated and spacious.

His saying: ﴿and a flowing spring﴾, meaning: having running water. It is also said: having springs flowing in it. It is said: "'anat" (the spring flowed) when water ran in it. They recited verse concerning al-Ma'in (the flowing water):

(Indeed those who departed from your heart left behind, and the flowing (spring) of your eye never ceases to flow.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 23, verse 51:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things and do righteous deeds﴾. Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Suddi and a group of scholars said: The intended meaning of His saying ﴿O messengers﴾ is Muhammad (ﷺ). The Arabs mention the plural while meaning the singular, for they say to a man: "O people, stop your harm to us." Others said: The intended meaning is all the messengers. Some of them said: The intended meaning is Isa (peace be upon him), as if He said: "We said to Isa: O messengers." It has been narrated from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O people, God does not accept except what is good, and God has commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers, so He said: ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things and do righteous deeds﴾, and He said to the believers: ﴿O you who have believed, eat of the good things We have provided for you and be grateful to God﴾." Then he mentioned a man, disheveled and dusty, who raises his hands to the sky and says: "O Lord, O Lord," while his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful, and he has been nourished with the unlawful. How then should he be answered?"

In the narrative: Isa used to eat from his mother's spinning. Eating (al-akl) is taking a thing into the mouth so that it reaches the stomach after chewing. As for His saying ﴿of the good things﴾, it means: of the lawful (al-halal). His saying ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾: righteousness (al-salah) is steadfastness upon what the Sharia (the revealed law) requires.

His saying ﴿Indeed, I am Knowing of what you do﴾: this is an exhortation to perform obedience, meaning: do righteous deeds, for I will recompense you for your deeds.

Almighty God says: ﴿And indeed this, your community, is one community﴾, meaning: your religion is one religion. It was also said: your law (shari'ah) is one law. And it is said: I have commanded you with what I commanded those before you, of the prophets and messengers, so your command is one.

And His words: ﴿And I am your Lord, so fear Me﴾, meaning: beware of Me.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 53:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿But they split their affair among themselves into sects﴾, meaning: they divided into Jews, Christians, Sabians and Magians. ﴿Scriptures﴾, meaning: pieces. Mujahid said: ﴿Zubur﴾ means books, meaning they made their books into pieces, and its meaning is: they believed in some of it and disbelieved in some of it, they altered some of it and did not alter some of it.

And His saying: ﴿Every faction, in what they have, rejoicing﴾, meaning: pleased.

It means that every group is pleased with what they have: the people of faith are pleased with faith and following the Prophet (ﷺ), and the disbelievers are pleased with their disbelief and opposition to the Prophet (ﷺ).

"His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So leave them in their bewilderment for a time﴾ means: in their misguidance. It is also said: in their blindness.

And His saying: ﴿for a time﴾ means: until they die, and the verse is a threat."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 55:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Do they reckon that by giving them wealth and children﴾ ... the verse. Its meaning: Do they reckon that what We provide them as a supply of wealth and children

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 56:

﴿We hasten for them in good things﴾. That is: We hasten for them in good things and advance them as reward for them, (as) approval of their deeds. The real meaning is that: the matter is not as they suppose, that wealth and children are good for them; rather it is a gradual leading-on (istidraj) for them and a deception (makr) against them. This is the meaning of His Exalted saying: ﴿Nay, they do not perceive﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 57:

Allah's words: ﴿Indeed, those who are, out of fear of their Lord, apprehensive﴾. Al-khashya (fear, reverential awe): the agitation of the soul at what is anticipated of harm. Al-ishfaq here is the fear of punishment. So the meaning of the verse is: the believers, out of fear of their Lord, do not feel secure from His punishment. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "The believer combines good deeds and fear, while the hypocrite combines bad deeds and a sense of security."

"And those who believe in the signs of their Lord" — that is, they affirm them as true.

Wait, let me translate faithfully as required, with the Qur'anic quotation kept in the ﴿ ﴾ markers:

His saying: ﴿And those who believe in the signs of their Lord﴾ — meaning: they affirm (them) as true.
"The words of Allah Most High: ﴿And those who do not associate anything with their Lord﴾ — its meaning is well known."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 23, verse 60:

His statement, the Exalted: ﴿And those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful﴾. It is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he recited: "And those who come with what they came with" (wa-alladhina ya'tuna ma ataw bihi), and this was the recitation of ʿĀ'isha (may Allah be pleased with her).

(And His statement: ﴿give what they give﴾ means: they give what they have given. And the reading: "come with what they came with" means: they do what they have done.)

And His statement: ﴿and their hearts are fearful﴾ means: fearful.

And His statement: ﴿that they will return to their Lord﴾. That is: because they will return to their Lord. Its meaning: they feared because they knew that their return is to their Lord. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Saʿid ibn Wahb narrated from ʿĀ'isha (may Allah be pleased with her) that she said to the Prophet: "O Messenger of Allah, regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful﴾, are they the ones who steal and drink wine while their hearts are fearful?" He said: "No, O daughter of the Truthful (al-Siddiq), rather they are those who pray, fast, and give charity, while their hearts are fearful that it will not be accepted from them." In another narration: "and they fear that it will not be accepted from them."

The Shaykh al-Imam said: Abu ʿAli al-Shafiʿi informed us of this hadith, saying: Abu al-Hasan Ibn [Firas] informed us: Abu Muhammad ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Muqri' informed us: my grandfather Muhammad related to us, from Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna, who said: Malik ibn Mughawwal informed us, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Saʿid ibn Wahb... the report.

And al-Hasan al-Basri said: "By Allah, they worked at acts of obedience, strove in them, and feared that they would be rejected." This is the well-known view regarding the verse. The second view: the intended meaning of the verse is that they committed acts of disobedience while fearing Allah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 61:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿They hasten towards the good things, and they are foremost in them﴾. That is: they are foremost towards them.

The poet said:

(My she-camel swerves away from the direction of al-Yamama, and she did not aim from its people for your sake)

That is: towards your sake. And it is said: "they are foremost in them (lahā sābiqūn)" means: for their sake they are foremost. A person says to another: "I intended this town for you (laka)", meaning: for your sake. And it is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: ﴿And they are foremost in them﴾ means: happiness from Allah has preceded for them.

The Quran says: "And We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity" (﴿وَلَا نكلف نفسا إِلَّا وسعهَا﴾). The meaning has already been explained. It is also said: We did not obligate the sick person to pray standing, nor the poor person to pay zakat and perform Hajj, nor the traveler to fast, and similar things.

And His saying: "And with Us is a Book which speaks with truth" (﴿ولدينا كتاب ينْطق بِالْحَقِّ﴾) means: with Us is a Book that speaks with truth, and it is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). Some scholars have used this verse as evidence that whoever writes a letter to a person has spoken to him (kallamahu).

And His saying: "which speaks with truth" (﴿ينْطق بِالْحَقِّ﴾) means: it reports with truthfulness.

And His saying: "and they will not be wronged" (﴿وهم لَا يظْلمُونَ﴾) means: their rights will not be diminished.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 63:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nay, their hearts are in confusion about this﴾, meaning: in a covering. It is said: "So-and-so was overwhelmed by water" (ghamarahu al-ma'), meaning: it covered him.

And His saying: ﴿And they have deeds other than that which they are doing﴾ (in this there are two opinions: that the disbelievers have evil deeds decreed against them besides what they have done, ﴿which they are doing﴾). This is the view of Mujahid and a group, while Qatadah said: the verse refers to the people of obedience, and its meaning is that the believers have deeds other than the good they have done, ﴿which they are doing﴾. And the first view is more apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 64:

Allah's words: ﴿Until when We seize their affluent ones with the punishment﴾ — we have already explained the meaning of al-mutraf (the affluent, those given to luxury and ease).

And His words: ﴿with the punishment﴾ — this refers to the sword on the day of Badr. It is also said: it is the famine (al-qahṭ) which befell them through the supplication of the Prophet (ﷺ).

And His words: ﴿when they cry out for help﴾ — meaning: they shout and seek relief.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 65:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Do not cry out today﴾ mean: do not shout today. Al-judar (crying out, lamentation) is raising the voice.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, you will not be helped by Us﴾ mean: there is no one who will prevent Us from punishing you. It has also been said that ﴿will not be helped﴾ means: will not be provided for (will not be given sustenance). It is said: "a land that is manṣūrah," meaning: one that has been rained upon.

Almighty Allah's saying: ﴿Indeed, My verses were recited to you, but you turned back on your heels, retreating﴾. That is: you would turn back backward upon your heels. It is also said: the ugliest of walking is returning backward on one's heels.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 67:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Proudly, [dismissing it] by it﴾ — the scholars have differed regarding His saying. The most apparent of the opinions is that what is meant by it is the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram); it is also said that it means the House (al-Bayt), i.e., they were exalting themselves by the Sacred House. Their self-exaltation was that they used to say: "We are the people of God and the neighbours of His House," while the rest of the Arabs were in fear and they were in security. This is the statement of Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and a group [of scholars]. The second opinion: ﴿proudly, [dismissing it] by it﴾, i.e., by the Qur'an, in the sense that they were arrogant and therefore did not believe in it. The third opinion: that it refers to the Messenger, in the sense we mentioned regarding the Qur'an.

And His saying: ﴿telling tales at night﴾ — it is read in the irregular (shadhdh) reading as "sammaran." The words al-samir (al-sāmir) and al-sammar (al-simar) have the same meaning in the language (lughah). The verse refers to their sitting at night around the House, conversing in the evening (yasmurun). Al-Thawri said: "al-samar" is the shade of the moon. The Arabs say: "I will not speak to you, al-samar and al-qamar," meaning: night and day.

And His saying: ﴿Talking nonsense﴾ — i.e., turning away from the Prophet, from faith in him, and from the Qur'an and faith. It is also said: ﴿tahjurun﴾ means "you rave" (tahdhun). It is read as "tahjurun" from hijr in speech, which is foul speech. In the narrations it is reported that they used to sit near the House in the shade of the moon and revile the Prophet (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 68:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not pondered over the word?﴾ That is: what has come to them of the word, which is the Qur'an.

And His saying: ﴿Or has there come to them that which did not come to their forefathers of old?﴾ (That is: do they suppose that there has come to them what had not come to those before them? Its meaning is: We sent to them a messenger just as We sent to the former peoples.)

Almighty Allah's saying: ﴿Or did they not recognize their Messenger, so that they deny him?﴾ That is: they knew him as a child and as a man, they knew his lineage, they knew his faithfulness to covenants, his fulfilling of trusts, and his truthfulness in speech. He is Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, as we mentioned before.

Almighty God says: ﴿Or do they say, "There is madness in him"?﴾ That is, "jinn" (madness).

And His words: ﴿Nay, he has brought them the truth﴾ meaning, "with truth" (sincerity). And His words: ﴿but most of them are averse to the truth﴾ meaning, "they are displeased (sakhitun)."

The Exalted said: ﴿And if the truth had followed their desires﴾ meaning: if what was revealed of the Qur'an had followed their desires.

﴿The heavens and the earth would have been corrupted, and whoever is in them﴾ He said this because they wished that Allah, the Exalted, would reveal the mention of their idols according to what they believed about them, and because it is in the sense of His saying: ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined﴾. In the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud it is: "The heavens and the earth would have been corrupted, and whoever is in them, and whoever created them."

The second opinion regarding the verse: the intended meaning of ﴿the truth﴾ is Allah, the Exalted, and its meaning is: if Allah had followed their desires, He would have named for Himself a partner and a son, and the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been corrupted.

His saying: ﴿Rather, We have brought them their reminder﴾ means: We have brought them that which causes them to be mindful, and it is said: their honour. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people﴾, meaning: an honour for you and your people.

His saying: ﴿But they, from their reminder, are turning away﴾ means: they are turning away from their honour and from that which would remind them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 72:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Or do you ask them for a payment?﴾ It is also read as "kharajan" (خراجا), and both mean a recompense and a wage. It is related from Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' that he said: "The kharaj (خراج, tax or levy) is on land, and the kharj (خرج, payment) is on necks."

And His words: ﴿But the payment of your Lord﴾ means: His reward, ﴿is better﴾ means: the wage of your Lord is better.

And His words: ﴿And He is the best of providers﴾ means: the best of those who give.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 73:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed, you invite them to a straight path﴾. That is: to the religion of truth.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are deviating from the path.﴾ That is: they are turning away from the way of truth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 75:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And even if We had mercy upon them and removed what afflicted them of adversity﴾. It is narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) supplicated against Quraysh, saying: "O Allah, make for them years like the years of Yusuf." So drought and famine struck them, until they ate al-'Ilhiz, which is blood mixed with wool. Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse: {And even if We had mercy upon them and removed what afflicted them of adversity}, meaning: the hunger and the famine.

And His saying: ﴿They would persist in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾, meaning: they pressed on in their transgression, wandering blindly, and did not desist from it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 76:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And We indeed seized them with punishment﴾ — concerning this there are two opinions. One: that it is the sword on the day of Badr. The other: that it is hunger and famine. It is related that when the Prophet (ﷺ) invoked (a curse) upon his people, Abu Sufyan came to him and said: "O Muhammad, do you not claim that you were sent as a mercy to the worlds?" He said: "Yes." Abu Sufyan said to him: "You have killed the fathers by the sword, and destroyed the sons by hunger, so pray for us that this famine be lifted from us." So he prayed, and it was lifted from them.

And His words: ﴿Yet they did not humble themselves before their Lord, nor did they supplicate﴾ — that is: they did not submit and were not humbled before their Lord. And istikana (استكانة, humbling oneself) is the seeking of stillness (submission).

And His words: ﴿nor did they supplicate﴾ — that is: they did not beseech their Lord, but rather persisted in their defiance and rebellion.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 77:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Until, when We open upon them a gate of severe punishment﴾. It is said: [this refers to] death. And it is said: [it refers to] the establishment of the Hour.

And His saying: ﴿Then they will be in it despairing﴾. That is: bewildered and hopeless.

And from al-Suddi, who said: ﴿Until, when We open upon them a gate of severe punishment﴾ is the conquest of Makkah. And it is said: the severe punishment is illnesses and hardships. And from Mujahid, who said: it is the killing on the Day of Badr.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 78:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And it is He who produced for you hearing and sight and hearts﴾ — meaning, the faculties (al-asma') of hearing, so that you may hear; and this (al-sam') is singular in form but has the sense of the plural. And His words: ﴿and sight﴾ — meaning, so that you may see. And His words: ﴿and hearts﴾ — so that you may understand. And His words: ﴿little is it that you give thanks﴾ — meaning, you do not give thanks for these blessings.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And it is He who multiplied you upon the earth, and to Him you will be gathered.﴾ That is: He created you, spread you abroad, and made you numerous upon the earth. As for His words ﴿And to Him you will be gathered﴾, that means: you will be resurrected.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 80:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is He who gives life and causes death, and His is the alternation of the night and the day﴾. That is: the governance of the night and the day in their increase and decrease. And it is said: among it is the alternation (ikhtilaf) of the night and the day.

And His saying ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾. Its meaning: will you not reason about the signs which He has placed in them.
Allah's saying, ﴿Rather, they said the like of what the former ones said﴾ — its meaning: they denied, just as the former ones denied.

"Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They say: 'When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be raised up?'﴾ That is, shall we be gathered (for judgment). They said this in the manner of denial and astonishment."

"The word of Allah Most High: ﴿Indeed we and our fathers have been promised this before. This is nothing but the fables of the ancients.﴾ That is: the lies of the ancients. It is also said: their evening tales and their stories. And it was said: what the ancients inscribed in their books, with no reality to it."
The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Say: "To whom belong the earth and whoever is in it, if you should know?"﴾ The meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 85:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They will say, "To Allah."﴾ That is, it belongs to Allah, and it is His dominion.

And His saying: ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾ That is, will you not take heed?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 86:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Mighty Throne?﴾ That is: the great couch (sarir).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 87:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿They will say, "To Allah."﴾ It is also recited: "They will say, Allah."

As for His words, "They will say, Allah," this refers to the wording (lafz). The meaning is like a man who says to another: "Whose house is this?" and he replies: "Zayd's."

As for His words, ﴿They will say, "To Allah."﴾ this refers to the meaning rather than the wording, just as a speaker says to another: "Whose house is this?" and he replies: "It belongs to Zayd."

And His words, ﴿Say, "Will you not then be mindful?"﴾ mean: will you not then take heed (tahdharun)?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 88:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: In whose hand is the dominion (malakut) of everything﴾. That is: the Owner of everything. The taa' (ta') here is for emphasis (li-l-mubalaghah), and likewise the pattern fa'lut is mentioned for emphasis, such as their saying: jabarut (majesty) and rahbut (dread). From their speech: "Rahbut is better than rahmut," and its meaning: that you be feared is better than that you be shown mercy.

And His saying: ﴿And He protects, and none can be protected against Him﴾ means: He gives security to all people, and no one gives security against Him. Its meaning: whomever Allah grants security, no one can harm him, and whomever Allah does not grant security, no one can grant him security. It was also said: whoever Allah wills to punish, no one can prevent the punishment from him, and whoever wishes to punish another of the creation, Allah has power to prevent him from it. And His saying: ﴿If you know﴾ is clear in meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 89:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They will say, "To Allah." Say, "Then how are you deluded?"﴾ That is, you are deceived. It was also said: you are turned away from the truth. Al-Hasan said: its meaning is, where have your intellects gone? Abu 'Ubaydah said: ﴿Then how are you deluded?﴾ means you wander blindly (ta'ammuh).

Almost all of the text is Qur'anic quotation or commentary. Translating:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Rather, We have brought them the truth, and indeed they are liars﴾. That is, with the truth; indeed they are liars in what they ascribe to Allah of partners and offspring.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 91:

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Allah has not taken any son, nor has there been with Him any god﴾, meaning: any partner. And His saying: ﴿Otherwise, each god would have taken away what he created﴾, meaning: He would have been singular in what He created, and so would not have accepted that His creation and His favour be attributed to another. And His saying: ﴿And some of them would have overcome others﴾. Meaning: some of them would seek to overpower the others, as the kings of the world do among themselves. Then He declared Himself free of what they describe, saying: ﴿Glory be to Allah above what they describe﴾.

Almighty God's saying: ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾, that is: the secret and the open.

And His saying: ﴿Exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾, that is: He is glorified above what they associate with Him, and its meaning is that He is greater than to be described by this attribute.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 93:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: My Lord, if You should show me that which they are promised﴾. He means: if You should show me the punishment You promised them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 94:

﴿My Lord, do not place me among the wrongdoing people.﴾ That is: make me outside of them, and do not punish me along with them. Thus al-Zajjaj mentioned it. The people of tafsir (ahl al-tafsir) said: This is evidence that it is permissible for the servant to ask Allah, exalted is He, for what is certainly going to happen (ma huwa ka'in la mahala).

"Hadith" not present; this is a short tafsir passage. Translate faithfully.

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And indeed We are able to show you that which We promise them.﴾ That is: of the punishment that We promise them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 96:

The words of God, Exalted is He: ﴿Repel evil with that which is better﴾. Most of the people of tafsir (exegesis) hold that what is meant by it is repelling [evil] through patience, bearing harm, and refraining from fighting, and this [ruling] came before the verse of the sword (ayat al-sayf). It is narrated from a group of the Followers (al-tabi'un) that they said: it means that one greets with salam the one who harms him, so the repelling is by greeting him with salam. It is narrated from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: it is repelling shirk with "there is no god but God" (la ilaha illa Allah). And it is narrated from some of them: it is repelling the evil (munkar) with admonition (al-mawi'ah).

The words of God, Exalted is He: ﴿We are most knowing of what they describe﴾. That is: of their description and their lying.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And say, "My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the whisperings of the devils."﴾ [meaning] their insinuations (wasawis). In the language, hamz (pressing, prodding) is derived from pushing (al-daf'), and the devil's pushing of others toward disobedience happens through his whispering. Thus it is known that the hamzat are the insinuations. It has also been said: the hamz of the devil is his inciting (ighra'uhu) to disobedience.

And His saying: ﴿And I seek refuge with You, my Lord, from their presence﴾ — meaning, lest they attend to my affairs. He mentioned "presence" only because the devil incites one to disobedience and whispers to one when he is present.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 99:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Until, when death comes to one of them﴾, means: death attends one of them. And His saying: ﴿He says, "My Lord, send me back"﴾ has two opinions. The first: it is addressed to the angels, namely the angels who attend to the seizing of the soul. This is a weak view, because he said: ﴿My Lord﴾.

As for the second view, which is the well-known one: the address is to God, and it is as if the disbeliever asks his Lord at the time of death to return him to the world. If it is said: how can this be consistent, when he said: ﴿send me back﴾, and a single person is not addressed with the plural form, and it is not appropriate for a speaker to say, "O God, forgive us [plural]" for himself? The answer to this: the plural was used only as a form of majesty and exaltation, for God, may He be exalted, speaks of Himself in the plural, saying: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed We are its guardians﴾, and the like of this is abundant in the Qur'an. So His saying ﴿send me back﴾ is in accord with this, as one addresses a group. It is reported from al-Khalil that he was asked about this verse, and he was extremely cautious in speaking about the Qur'an, and he said: ﴿My Lord, send me back﴾ means: make me one who is returned.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 100:

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿So that I may do righteous deeds in what I have left behind.﴾ That is: "I say: there is no god but Allah." It was also said: it refers to doing acts of obedience. Qatadah said: he sought to be returned in order to act righteously, not in order to gather worldly goods and fulfil desires. So may Allah have mercy on the person who acts in the way the disbeliever wishes to act when he sees the punishment.

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿No! It is but a word he utters.﴾ It means: the request for a return. The scholars among the early generations (al-salaf) said: no servant who has even an atom's weight of good with Allah asks for a return, for if he has good with Allah, he loves to meet Him. They agreed that the request for a return is made by the disbeliever, not by the believer.

And His saying: ﴿And behind them is a barrier (barzakh)﴾ That is: a barrier (ḥājiz), and it is the grave.

And His saying: ﴿until the Day they are resurrected.﴾ So the barzakh is what lies between death and resurrection (al-ba'th). It is also said: it is what lies between this world (al-dunya) and the Hereafter (al-akhirah).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 101:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When the Trumpet is blown﴾. It is related from al-Hasan al-Basri that he said: "That is, into the Trumpet." This is a weak view. The sound position is that the Trumpet (al-Sur) is a horn into which Israfil will blow. It is well known that the Prophet said: "How can I be at ease, when the holder of the horn has put the horn to his mouth, bent his forehead, and inclined his ear, waiting to be commanded so that he may blow?"

Among the scholars are those who say that there will be three blasts: a blast of terror (al-Sa'q), a blast of death, and a blast of resurrection. Most of them hold that there will be two blasts: a blast of death and a blast of resurrection, and that al-Sa'q is death itself. There will be forty years between the two blasts.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿so there will be no kinship among them that day﴾, that is, there will be no kinship through which they boast and connect with one another. As for the essence of kinship, it remains.

As for the saying of the Prophet, upon him be prayers and peace: "Every cause and every lineage will be cut off except my cause and my lineage," the meaning is that no cause or lineage will benefit on the Day of Resurrection except my cause and my lineage. It is said: "His cause is the Qur'an, and his lineage is faith."

His saying: ﴿and they will not ask one another﴾, that is, they will not ask one another with the question of connection. If it is said: Did not Allah, exalted is He, say: ﴿Then some of them will turn to others, questioning one another﴾?

The answer: It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "The Day of Resurrection has stations and moments. In one station the fear will be so severe that their minds will be bewildered (fa-tadhhalu), so they will not ask one another; and in another place they will regain consciousness, and so they will ask one another."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 102:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then whoever's scales are heavy, those are the successful.﴾ That is: the victorious and the saved.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And whoever's scales are light, those are the ones who have lost their souls﴾, meaning: they defrauded themselves through destruction (the verse). And His saying: ﴿in Hell, they will abide eternally﴾, meaning: they will remain.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 104:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿The Fire will scorch their faces﴾. Al-lafh (scorching) is stronger than al-nafh (blowing). Its meaning: the heat of the Fire strikes their faces. It has also been said: the Fire burns their faces and cooks them.

And His words: ﴿and they will be therein grim-faced﴾. Al-kalih (grim-faced) in the language means the one who frowns. As for what is related in the tafsir, it is the one whose lips have drawn back and whose teeth have become exposed.

It is related from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Like a roasted head, its teeth exposed and its lips drawn back."

Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi mentioned in his Jami', with a narration from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said concerning this verse: "It is that his upper lip shrinks until it reaches the middle of his head, and his lower lip hangs down until it strikes his navel." In some tafsirs: "and his teeth protrude from his lips [forty] cubits."

It is related from one of the Successors (tabi'un) among those who feared (God): that he passed by roasting meat and saw sheep heads that had been exposed; when he looked at them he fainted, as if he were recalling this verse.

The Quran verse quoted here is 23:105, and the phrase "قوله تعالى" should be rendered as the Most High's words.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Were not My verses recited to you, and did you not used to deny them?﴾ That is: you would reject and disavow them.

"And His saying: ﴿They will say, "Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us, and we were a people astray."﴾ It is also read "shaqawatuna" (شقاوتنا), and the two mean the same thing. What is meant is: He only caused us to enter the Fire because of what Your decree and Your judgment overpowered upon us, by our wretchedness. And His saying: ﴿and we were a people astray﴾ means: astray from the truth."

Allah the Exalted's saying: ﴿Our Lord, bring us out of it, and if we return, then indeed we are wrongdoers﴾. Then He leaves them for a period equal to the lifespan of the world; and in another narration: twice the lifespan of the world.

Then He says: ﴿[He will say:] "Be driven away into it, and do not speak to Me."﴾ He said: Then their hope will be cut off at that time, and nothing will be heard from them after that except groaning and sighing. As for His saying ﴿Be driven away﴾, it means: go far away, and it is like the saying of the Arabs: "I drove the dog away (khasa'tu al-kalb)," meaning: I made it go away.

**The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, there was a group of My servants who said, "Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of the merciful."﴾** The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: this refers to Bilal, Salman, Ammar, Suhayb, and the poor among the Companions of the Messenger.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 110:

And His saying: ﴿So you took them in derision﴾. It is also recited as "sukhriyyan" (sikhriyyan). So His saying ﴿sukhriyyan﴾ is from mockery (al-istihzaʾ), and His saying "sikhriyyan" is from subjugation (al-taskhir).

And His saying: ﴿until they caused you to forget My remembrance﴾. That is, you occupied yourselves with mocking them and ridiculing them, and you abandoned My remembrance, while it was obligatory upon you to remember Me instead of mocking them.

And His saying: ﴿while you used to laugh at them﴾. In this verse there is evidence that mocking people is a grave sin, and that it incurs a threat (of punishment). It is related from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: "Whoever laughs a single burst of laughter from heedlessness of knowledge (ʿilm), it will never return to him, ever."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 111:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, I have rewarded them today for their patience; indeed, it is they who are the triumphant.﴾ That is, for their patience (ṣabr). ﴿Indeed, it is they who are the triumphant.﴾ That is, the saved (al-nājūn).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 112:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He will say, "How many years did you remain on the earth?"﴾. That is: Allah, exalted is He, says to the disbelievers: ﴿How many years did you remain on the earth?﴾ (i.e., in the world; it is also said: in the graves). It was recited as "Say (qul): how many years did you remain on the earth?" and its meaning is: Say, O disbeliever.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 113:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They will say, "We stayed a day or part of a day."﴾ They only mentioned "a day or part of a day" because they forgot the number of what they had stayed, due to the terror of what confronts them on the Day of Resurrection. If someone says: this verse indicates that the punishment of the grave is not established for the disbelievers, because if it were established they would not have said, "We stayed a day or part of a day"? The answer to this is in two respects. The first: the punishment of the grave has left their hearts due to the terror of what confronts them on the Day of Resurrection. The second: Allah, the Exalted, lifts the punishment from the people of the graves between the two blasts (al-nafkhatayn), so they forget the punishment of the grave and find rest, and it is only for this that they say, "We stayed a day or part of a day."

And His saying: ﴿So ask those who count﴾ means: the angels who know the number of what they stayed.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 114:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He will say, "You remained only a little, if only you had known."﴾ That is: you remained only a little. ﴿If only you had known﴾ means: if only you knew the number of the years you remained. He mentioned "a little" because the individual of the people of the world, even if he remains in the world for many years, will be but a little compared to what he remains in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 115:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Did you think that We had created you in vain?﴾ That is, "so that you would play or act frivolously." Allah, exalted is He, has also called the whole of the worldly life play and amusement, saying: ﴿Know that the life of this world is but play and amusement﴾. Thus the verse indicates that the human being was not created to pursue this world and occupy himself with it, but rather was created to worship Allah and to carry out His commands. It is related from some of them that he said: ﴿Did you think that We had created you in vain?﴾ has the same meaning as His words, exalted is He: ﴿Does man think that he will be left neglected?﴾, and its meaning is that He does not leave His command unattended. Some of them said: "He created [you] for the ruin (halak) of eternity, or for the dominion of eternity."

As for His words: ﴿and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾, its meaning is apparent.

Allah's saying, the Exalted: ﴿So exalted is Allah, the True King; there is no god but Him, the Lord of the Noble Throne﴾. That is, the Highly Exalted. It has also been said: the Good. We have already explained the meaning of ﴿Exalted﴾ earlier.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 117:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever calls upon another god along with Allah, of which he has no proof﴾, meaning: he has no evidence or argument for it. The scholars said: there is no argument for anyone in claiming associating partners with Allah (shirk); rather, the argument is against them.

His saying: ﴿Then his reckoning is only with his Lord﴾. This is in the sense of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then indeed, upon Us is their reckoning﴾. It is related that a Bedouin (a‘rabi) came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Who will call us to account on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "Allah." He said: "We are saved, by the Lord of the Ka'bah! Indeed, when the Generous One has the power, He forgives." And the report is gharib (rare, weak in chain).

His saying: ﴿Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed﴾, meaning: they will not attain happiness and will not win.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 23, verse 118:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And say: "My Lord, forgive and have mercy, for You are the best of the merciful."﴾

﴿Forgive﴾: conceal (istur). ﴿And have mercy﴾: show compassion (i'tataf). Al-Ghafur means the one who conceals, and al-Rahim is the one who is compassionate (al-'Attuf).

His words: ﴿And You are the best of the merciful﴾. That is: the best of those who have shown mercy.
